title: Compass and Wreck
premise: Desert ranger Cyrus Quintana, who has spent a decade erasing herself from every record, tracks a thief into a dead riverbed and finds a salvage chest stamped with the seal of Vessia, a drowned nation officially erased from all maps. The chest holds a compass that points not north but toward the river's forbidden source, and the thief she was chasing turns out to be a Vessian survivor who needs it to reach a sanctuary before the monsoon seals the high country for a year. Hunted by a survey company that wants the seal destroyed and shadowed by the ranger service she abandoned, Cyrus must choose between the invisibility she built and the found family forming around her. In the end she reaches the source, learns the sanctuary is the thief's scattered people rather than a place, and burns her own ranger records to walk into the mountains with them as the monsoon breaks.
about_author: Rafael Galloway is a former river guide who spent six seasons running freight through canyon country before turning to writing full-time. His novels are known for austere prose, merciless landscapes, and characters who find family in the unlikeliest company.

chapters.title: The Thief in the Dry Country
chapters.summary: Cyrus Quintana, a desert ranger who has carefully unmade her official identity, picks up the trail of a thief who stole from a supply depot. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: competent solitude, her satisfaction in a landscape that asks nothing of her but survival.

chapters.title: What the River Gave Back
chapters.summary: Following the trail to a seasonal river, Cyrus finds the thief's abandoned camp and, wedged in the silt, a bronze-stamped chest bearing the seal of Vessia, a nation drowned and stricken from records forty years ago. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: unease; the past surfacing like a body.

chapters.title: The Compass That Lies About North
chapters.summary: Inside the chest: documents, a seal ring, and a brass compass whose needle swings toward the river's upstream source. The thief, a young man named Ede, doubles back to reclaim it and is caught. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: reluctant curiosity overriding her instinct to walk away.

chapters.title: Prisoner of the Sandwash
chapters.summary: Cyrus interrogates Ede, who claims to be Vessian and says the compass leads to a sanctuary above the source where survivors of the drowning still live. She doesn't believe him, but the survey company's drones overhead change her mind about letting him go. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: suspicion warring with a protectiveness she resents.

chapters.title: The Survey Company
chapters.summary: A company retrieval team led by the courteous, ruthless Odile Marsh reaches the ranger station asking questions about a seal-stamped chest. Cyrus lies smoothly, then realizes her forged records have been flagged. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: the trap closing on the invisibility she spent a decade building.

chapters.title: Upstream
chapters.summary: Cyrus and Ede flee into the canyon system, following the river upstream. He teaches her Vessian river-signs carved into old walls, and she realizes the drowned nation mapped this country better than her own ever did. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: first fragile trust; the landscape becoming a shared language.

chapters.title: Ede
chapters.summary: A slower chapter: Ede tells how he was smuggled out at six years old, the only child of his family to survive the flooding of the Vessian valleys. He carries the seal ring for people he can barely remember. POV: Cyrus observing, with Ede's account in his own voice. Emotional beat: grief given a shape; Cyrus recognizing her own self-erasure in his exile.

chapters.title: The Third Traveler
chapters.summary: They discover someone has been following them for two days: Sefa, an aging Vessian woman who has spent decades walking circuits of the old country and knows the source route. She joins them uninvited. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: prickly friction becoming, against Cyrus's will, something like company.

chapters.title: Marsh at the Confluence
chapters.summary: Marsh's team corners them at a confluence; in the escape Cyrus is wounded and loses her ranger credentials pack, meaning her real identity is now in company hands. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve; there is no invisible way out anymore.

chapters.title: The Price of Water
chapters.summary: In the high desert stretch, water runs short. Sefa's knowledge saves them, but a hard choice over rationing leaves Ede angry at Cyrus, who was ready to leave him behind for the group's survival. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh—survival has a price, and she has always been willing to pay it in other people.

chapters.title: Records
chapters.summary: A company checkpoint town: Cyrus sees her true service file displayed as a bounty, including the mission she abandoned years ago that got her partner killed. Ede reads it and says nothing, but something shifts between them. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: shame exposed; the family forming around her has seen the worst of her.

chapters.title: The Gorge of Bells
chapters.summary: Sefa leads them through a gorge hung with Vessian memorial bells, drowned-nation survivors' waymarkers. Marsh's team ambushes; Sefa is captured covering their escape. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: rage and guilt; the found family is being spent one member at a time.

chapters.title: The Bargain
chapters.summary: Cyrus considers trading the compass for Sefa, and for her own file. Ede refuses to let her, forcing her to admit she was looking for permission to quit. They plan a rescue instead. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: the choice between the old self that survives alone and the new one that doesn't.

chapters.title: Rescue at the Survey Camp
chapters.summary: A night rescue: Cyrus walks into Marsh's camp under a flag of parley, buys time with a false offer, and Ede and Sefa slip the cordon. Marsh lets them go—she wants them to lead her to the source. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: the cold clarity of being used, and using it.

chapters.title: Above the Tree Line
chapters.summary: The monsoon's edge arrives early; they climb into freezing high country racing the storms. Sefa, injured in the escape, begins to fail. She gives Cyrus the seal ring and asks her to carry the Vessians' memory whether or not she believes in it. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: inheritance accepted; belonging without permission.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: They reach the river's source: not a sanctuary but a valley of ruins and a small living settlement—Vessian descendants who never left, who have hidden for forty years. The compass was a test; it only points for those who already belong. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: awe and displacement—she has arrived somewhere she has no right to.

chapters.title: Marsh Descends
chapters.summary: Marsh's team, having followed the cleft in the storm, reaches the valley rim demanding the seal and the settlers' relocation under an old water-rights claim. The settlers prepare to scatter rather than fight. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: the dread of watching a family prepare to dissolve.

chapters.title: The Seal
chapters.summary: Cyrus proposes the impossible: the seal ring and the old water-rights documents prove the settlers hold the valley's claim under pre-drowning law. She will testify—under her real name, with her real record—as a serving ranger. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: the price of survival finally named as self-erasure, and refused.

chapters.title: Monsoon
chapters.summary: Marsh forces the confrontation as the monsoon breaks; in the flooding gorge, Cyrus's testimony and the settlers' documents turn Marsh's own corporate backers against the operation, and Marsh retreats rather than be disavowed. Sefa dies as the storm passes. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: catharsis bought at real cost; the river forgives nothing.

chapters.title: The Naming
chapters.summary: In the aftermath, the settlers ask Cyrus to stay for the winter sealing of the valley. She gives them her true name, the one no one has spoken in a decade, and it is entered in the valley's ledger. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: quiet, almost frightening peace.

chapters.title: What She Burned
chapters.summary: Cyrus descends once more, formally resigns her commission, and burns her remaining forged records at the ranger station—ending the double life for good. Marsh, watching from a distance, chooses not to report it. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: release; the old self laid down like a heavy pack.

chapters.title: Compass and Wreck
chapters.summary: Spring: Cyrus climbs back to the source valley with supplies, the compass rehung at the shrine where it points at whoever stands before it. Ede greets her at the gate. She is home, not because the valley needed her, but because she chose it. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: belonging earned, kept, and finally believed.
